meta.title: Statistical tests on the record
meta.description: Hypothesis tests on the data this dashboard publishes: whether the identified dead are confined to men of fighting age, whether killing continued through the ceasefires, whether the ICJ orders changed the daily death rate, the West Bank before and after 7 October 2023, the integrity of the Ministry of Health named list, and recognition of Palestine against governments calling it genocide.
meta.correction: p-values are adjusted for the false discovery rate (Benjamini-Hochberg, 5%) across all 15 tests run in the analysis.
meta.caution: A change in a series at a dated event is an association, not proof that the event caused it. Tests on the named list inherit any bias in who has been identified.

groups.H1: Who is killed: age and sex against the population
groups.H4: The West Bank before and after 7 October 2023

departures.text: The Ministry of Health daily series cannot be used for the pause: the Ministry had stopped reporting on 11 November, the Government Media Office issued no total during the pause, and the series records zero for every day of it, which are missing reports and not days without deaths. As directed by the editor, the pause-period count was reconstructed from the killings reported incident by incident in OCHA's flash updates and by the Associated Press and Al Jazeera (five deaths in seven days, a lower bound, since OCHA also reports shootings with 'several casualties' it does not break down). The comparison window is the 14 days before the pause, from the daily series. Because the two windows are measured differently, the test is repeated against an upper bound of 40 deaths, the rise in the Government Media Office total during the pause less the 160 bodies recovered from the rubble.

tests.title: Age and sex of the dead: pattern confined to men of fighting age
tests.null: The identified dead are confined to men aged 18-59.
tests.data: Ministry of Health named list, 72,835 identified dead; PCBS/UNFPA Gaza Strip population 2023 (2,226,544).
tests.test: Exact binomial test of the share of women, children and people aged 60 and over against zero

effect.name: Share of dead who are women, children under 18 or aged 60+

tests.reading: 52.1% of the identified dead (95% CI 51.7% to 52.5%) are women, children under 18 or people aged 60 and over, against 75.5% of the population. More than half of the dead fall outside the group from which armed men are drawn: the dead are not confined to men of fighting age.

tests.title: The November 2023 pause and the daily killing rate
tests.null: The daily rate of killing during the pause of 24-30 November 2023 equalled the rate in the 14 days before it.
tests.data: Comparison window: Ministry of Health / Government Media Office daily series (Tech For Palestine), 10-23 November 2023. Pause: killings reported incident by incident (OCHA Flash Updates #49-#55; AP; Al Jazeera).
tests.test: Negative binomial regression on a pause indicator, Newey-West errors (lag 7)

effect.name: Rate ratio, pause against the 14 days before

incidents.note: Two people shot dead returning north (AP, Al Jazeera, Gaza Ministry of Health; OCHA: at least one)
One man killed by tank fire east of Al-Maghazi (OCHA Flash Update #51)
Two people killed by Israeli fire in northern Gaza City (OCHA Flash Update #55)

sensitivity.name: Against the upper bound of 40 deaths during the pause

tests.reading: Reported killings fell from 284.4 a day in the fortnight before the pause to 0.71 a day during it (rate ratio 0.0025, 95% CI 0.0013 to 0.0047). Killing did not stop: at least 5 people were reported killed in the 7 days. Against the upper bound of 40 deaths the ratio is 0.0201, still a fall of about 98%.

tests.title: The January-March 2025 ceasefire and the daily killing rate
tests.null: The daily rate of new killings during the ceasefire (19 Jan 2025 to 17 Mar 2025) equalled the rate in the 60 days before it.
tests.data: Ministry of Health daily series (Tech For Palestine). Ceasefire days count new killings only where the Ministry separates them from bodies recovered.
tests.test: Negative binomial regression on a ceasefire indicator, Newey-West errors (lag 7)

effect.name: Rate ratio, ceasefire against the 60 days before

sensitivity.name: New killings only in both windows

tests.reading: New killings fell from 48.8 a day in the 60 days before to 7.28 a day during the ceasefire (rate ratio 0.149, 95% CI 0.051 to 0.44). Killing continued throughout: 422 new killings were reported in 58 days (95% CI 6.6 to 8.0 a day).

tests.title: The October 2025 ceasefire and the daily killing rate
tests.null: The daily rate of new killings during the ceasefire (10 Oct 2025 to 01 Oct 2026) equalled the rate in the 60 days before it.
tests.data: Ministry of Health daily series (Tech For Palestine). Ceasefire days count new killings only where the Ministry separates them from bodies recovered.
tests.test: Negative binomial regression on a ceasefire indicator, Newey-West errors (lag 7)

effect.name: Rate ratio, ceasefire against the 60 days before

sensitivity.name: New killings only in both windows

tests.reading: New killings fell from 96.1 a day in the 60 days before to 3.74 a day during the ceasefire (rate ratio 0.039, 95% CI 0.027 to 0.055). Killing continued throughout: 1,336 new killings were reported in 357 days (95% CI 3.54 to 3.95 a day).

tests.title: The ICJ order of 26 January 2024 and the daily killing rate
tests.null: No change in the level or the slope of daily deaths at the order of 26 January 2024.
tests.data: Ministry of Health daily series (Tech For Palestine), 1 December 2023 to 31 July 2024.
tests.test: Segmented negative binomial regression (trend, and a level and slope change at each order), Newey-West errors; joint Wald test of level and slope

effect.name: Rate ratio, level change at the order

tests.reading: No detectable change in the level or the trend of daily deaths at the order (level rate ratio 1.006, 95% CI 0.81 to 1.3; joint test p = 0.99). The order was not followed by a measurable fall in the rate of killing. This is the absence of a detectable change, not proof that the order had no effect on any conduct.

tests.title: West Bank killings before and after 7 October 2023
tests.null: The daily rate of Palestinians killed in the West Bank was the same after 7 October 2023 as before it, within 2023.
tests.data: OCHA via the report: 208 killed in 279 days (1 January-6 October 2023); 299 in 86 days (7 October-31 December 2023).
tests.test: Exact conditional test of two Poisson rates
tests.reading: Palestinians were killed in the West Bank at 3.48 a day after 7 October 2023 against 0.75 before it, 4.66 times the rate (95% CI 3.89 to 5.59), in a year that was already the deadliest on record before the war began.

tests.title: Settler incidents against Palestinians, 2024 against 2022
tests.null: The rate of settler incidents against Palestinians was the same in 2024 as in 2022.
tests.data: OCHA daily averages via the report: 2 a day in 2022, 7 a day in 2024.
tests.test: Exact conditional test of two Poisson rates on annual counts reconstructed from the daily averages

sensitivity.name: At the rounding bounds least favourable to rejection (2.5 and 6.5 a day)

tests.reading: Settler incidents ran at 3.5 times the 2022 rate in 2024 (95% CI 3.22 to 3.81), and at 2.6 times even at the rounding bounds least favourable to the finding.

tests.title: The identity numbers on the named list
tests.null: The identity numbers are valid Population Registry numbers (pass the check digit).
tests.data: Ministry of Health named list, 72,835 records.
tests.test: Share passing the check digit, with its interval; exact binomial test against the 10% expected of fabricated numbers; decision rule: validity rejected if under 99% pass

effect.name: Share of identity numbers with a valid check digit

tests.result: validity not rejected; the 10% fabrication benchmark is rejected
tests.reading: All 72,835 of the 72,835 identity numbers pass the Population Registry check digit, where fabricated numbers would pass about one time in ten. There are 0 duplicate identity numbers and 0 duplicate name-and-birth-date pairs, and the stated age agrees with the date of birth in 72,835 of 72,835 records. The list as published is consistent with registry data. These tests cannot detect a real identity number attached to someone who did not die; that question needs matching against other records.

tests.title: Age heaping on the named list
tests.null: Age reporting shows no more heaping on ages ending in 0 and 5 than a registry-based list would.
tests.test: Whipple's index (ages 23-62) on the UN scale, and Myers' blended index (ages 10-89), against the PCBS 2017 census
tests.reading: No age heaping: Whipple's index is 100.0 and Myers' index 0.85, against the 2017 census's 100 and 2.4. Ages on the list follow from registry dates of birth rather than estimates, which is what a list built from identity records, and not from guesses, should show.

tests.title: Recognition of Palestine and calling it genocide
tests.null: Whether a UN member state government has called it genocide is independent of whether it recognises Palestine.
tests.data: World positions dataset, 193 UN member states.
tests.test: Fisher's exact test (interval with Haldane correction for a zero cell)
tests.reading: 50 of 157 recognising states have a government that has called it genocide; none of the 36 non-recognising states has (odds ratio 34.29, with a correction for the empty cell).
